report:
Short answer: There is an interpretable difference. Model B (B−A positive) injects a strong early-position signal that steers the model toward vivid/sensational/headline-style adjectives and event-related tokens (e.g., "tragic", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", "timeless", "victims", "tragedy", "coming", "worst") — i.e., more attention-grabbing, newsy/dramatic wording — especially at the very first token(s) of a sequence.

Why I conclude that
- Spatial pattern: the L2-norm of the difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 in late layers (layers ~20–25, especially layer 25 pos0 = 322), with smaller but noticeable mass at pos1. That says the checkpoint difference mainly affects the residual representation used to produce/initiate continuations (the first-token / early-token decoding).
- Logit-lens evidence: the top vocabulary directions that these high-norm cells point to (layers ~18–25, pos0/pos1) are dominated by adjectives and headline/event words: "tragic", "tragedy", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", "vibrant", "timeless", "loud", "victims", "refugees", "coming", "worst", "refused", "blitz", etc. Earlier layers show some other tokens (e.g. "Sale", "rock", small function tokens), but the large late-layer signal maps to strongly descriptive/sensational lexical items.
- Functional interpretation: a late-layer, position-0 activation that points at those tokens is consistent with a bias that changes how the model begins continuations — favoring more vivid/sensational/headline-like word choices at the start of generated text.

Caveats / alternative explanations
- This could be a topical bias (Model B is slightly more tuned toward news/tragedy/media-style text) or a stylistic bias (more sensational/descriptive phrasing) — the evidence supports "newsy/sensational/adjectival" shift but does not uniquely pin down whether it's topic vs. style.
- I don't have the actual patchscope continuations here to directly show generated text, so the inference relies on the logit-lens directions and the very strong late-layer pos0 norm. That is fairly suggestive but not a proof of behavior in full-generation settings.

If you want, I can (a) try to synthesize patched continuations using the difference vector to show concrete generated outputs, or (b) search for tokens/contexts where this difference flips actual next-token probabilities to verify the behavioral effect.
